confirmed_blocking.summary: _outcome_list accepts a stored outcome whose id is not a string, so an outcome file with a list or object id passes the shape check and _store's set comprehension (line 335) raises TypeError outside the Gap handler, aborting the whole refresh instead of yielding an inaccessible gap for that run; a null id is silently accepted. The round-1 wrong-shape blocker is only partly removed.
confirmed_blocking.evidence: Judge probe on a scratch copy of HEAD: adding '{"outcomes": [{"id": []}]}', '{"outcomes": [{"id": {}}]}' and '{"outcomes": [{"id": null}]}' to LocalGapTests.test_wrong_shape_outcome_file_is_inaccessible gives ERROR TypeError "cannot use 'list' as a set element", ERROR TypeError "cannot use 'dict' as a set element", and FAIL (no gap reported) respectively. _outcome_list (232-239) checks only isinstance(o, dict) and "id" in o; _is_terminal's tuple membership does not hash, so it returns False and _store line 335 raises; refresh catches only Gap. The writer stores only string ids (check:/review:/state:). spec.md line 120, FR-012 (spec.md line 141: malformed outcome file -> inaccessible, other runs MUST still refresh), plan.md lines 170 and 177 (confirmed failure path 'malformed existing outcome file -> inaccessible'). Commit c6b03b6 claims a wrong-shape file now yields an inaccessible gap. ENG-17 (expected failure escapes as a crash), ENG-16, ENG-25; Confirmed test scope / ENG-1 (declared failure path not covered for id types). Rated high for consistency with round-1's confirmed rating of the same trigger class.
confirmed_blocking.fix: In _outcome_list, replace `"id" in o` with `isinstance(o.get("id"), str)` (keeping isinstance(o, dict)). Add '{"outcomes": [{"id": []}]}', '{"outcomes": [{"id": {}}]}' and '{"outcomes": [{"id": null}]}' to test_wrong_shape_outcome_file_is_inaccessible (they fail on current code, a valid Red), asserting the inaccessible gap, unchanged files and feature-y refreshed.

advisory.summary: ENG-17 (carried from round 1): an OSError while acquiring the outcomes lock escapes refresh as a traceback instead of a classified gap; _store catches only lock.LockHeld. Practical impact is limited to an unwritable factory home.
advisory.fix: Catch OSError alongside lock.LockHeld around _acquire_home_lock and raise Gap('inaccessible', ...); add a test planting a failing lock.acquire.

advisory.summary: (carried from round 1) _slug uses [^a-z0-9]+ while plan.md line 130, DESIGN.md line 310 and its own docstring specify runs outside [a-z0-9-], so 'build--test' collapses and 'Lint - test' collides with 'Lint / test'.
advisory.fix: Use [^a-z0-9-]+ as documented (or amend the documented rule) and add the distinguishing slug cases.

advisory.summary: ENG-6 (carried from round 1): add_feedback repeats add's backlog entry envelope and own-entry glob scan, so the entry schema and ownership refusal live in two writers that can drift.
advisory.fix: Optionally extract a shared entry-body builder and owned-entries scan used by add and add_feedback.

advisory.summary: ENG-24 (carried from round 1): outcomes per run and evidence links per feedback entry grow without a cap, and gh output is read unbounded; growth tracks real PR review volume, so practical risk is low.
advisory.fix: Optionally cap stored evidence links per entry and bound the gh read, reporting overflow as a gap.

advisory.summary: ENG-25 (carried from round 1): a branch containing '/' is joined into the outcome and feedback-entry file names, so that run is a reported gap on every refresh (classified, not a traversal).
advisory.fix: Derive the file-name component from a slug or hash of the branch, or reject separators up front as a classified gap.

advisory.summary: ENG-14 (carried from round 1): feedback imports commands (only for main_repo) while commands imports feedback, an import cycle that works only through partial-module tolerance.
advisory.fix: Resolve the main repository in commands.cmd_feedback and pass it into refresh, then drop feedback's import of commands.

advisory.summary: (carried from round 1) A successful refresh with no new outcomes never creates the run's outcome file, while spec.md line 119 says a missing file is created on the first successful refresh.
advisory.fix: Write the (possibly empty) outcome file on the first successful refresh, or amend the spec edge case to 'created on the first stored outcome'.

advisory.summary: ENG-3 (carried from round 1): unit T009 spans ed49088 and 1f8ef55; the later commit reopens the checked unit with its own valid Red line and no tasks.md change.
advisory.fix: No history change; record in the verification record that T009 spans both commits.
